unit.why: A narrative about R. Isaac Leib (the author's father) living in poverty in Zhidachov, R. Zvi of Zhidachov appointing him head of the rabbinical court, and later vowing that he would not die before his disciple became a recognized leader.

stories.start_quote: ודר בעיר פינטשוב ערך ד׳ או ה׳
stories.end_quote: מתפשט זיין בכל העולם כולו עכד״ק
stories.summary_en: R. Zvi of Zhidachov orders his beloved disciple R. Isaac Leib to settle in Zhidachov. When he hears that the family is starving, he has the community appoint him head of the rabbinical court with a salary. Later, when a local man distresses the disciple, R. Zvi rises at the Sabbath meal and swears he will not leave the world until Isaac Leib is a vessel of blessing whose teaching spreads throughout the world.

tags.why: R. Zvi's love for and care of his disciple is the core of the story
